## Highlights

See how an agent memory changed before you undo it.

- `bkmr history <id> -p`: each change of a memory as a unified diff, like `git log -p`
- `bkmr restore <hid> --dry-run`: the diff a restore would apply, without writing anything. It runs the same checks as the restore, so it fails where the restore would fail.

Diffs are colored on a terminal and plain when piped, so `| delta` works.

The first run migrates your database automatically, after writing a backup next to it (`<name>_backup_YYYYMMDD.db`). The migration rebuilds the `bookmarks` table and the full-text index, so allow free disk space of about twice the database size: one copy for the backup, one for the rebuild. Bookmarks, IDs and embeddings are kept, and nothing needs to be embedded again.

## Breaking: exit codes changed

Scripts can now tell a usage error from a runtime failure. Check any script that tests for a specific bkmr exit code.

| Code | Meaning | Before |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success | |
| 1 | Valid command, but the operation failed | 64 |
| 64 | Usage error or invalid config file | Argument parser errors exited 2 |
| 65 | `import-files` found a duplicate name without `--update` | Unchanged |
| 130 | Declined confirmation | 0 or 64 |

Leaving the fuzzy finder with Esc still exits 0.

## New

- `bkmr backfill --prune` removes stale vectors without embedding anything. Use `--dry-run` to preview. It cannot be combined with `--force`.

  Versions before 7.9.0 kept the vector when embedding was disabled, so those bookmarks stayed findable through semantic and hybrid search. Until now, the only way to remove them was `backfill --force`, which re-embeds everything. Pruning also removes vectors whose bookmark no longer exists.

## Fixes

- The `--force` help text no longer claims that `_importe

- **An invalid config file is now fatal.** A config file that cannot be read or parsed stops bkmr with exit code 64. It used to be ignored, so bkmr silently continued with the defaults, including the default database. This also applies to `bkmr lsp`, where editors may only report that the server failed to start. `bkmr --generate-config` still works, to recover.
